ep01.title: Death for Apartments
ep01.logline: Moscow, summer 1993. Lonely owners of privatized apartments vanish one after another, and their homes are sold with flawless paperwork.
ep01.b03.title: Part One. The City
ep01.b05.title: Part Two. The Report
ep01.b06.title: Part Three. Paperwork
ep01.b08.title: Part Four. The Archive
ep01.b10.title: Part Five. Six Folders
ep01.b12.title: Part Six. The Interrogation
ep01.s01.l001: The residents of the building on Molodogvardeyskaya Street did not notice at first that the third-floor windows had stopped lighting up in the evenings.
ep01.s01.l002: Zoya Pavlovna? Zoya Pavlovna, are you home? I brought you some milk.
ep01.s01.l003: Strangers opened the door. They had keys, papers and a housing warrant. Zoya Pavlovna had nothing left at all.
ep01.s03.l001: In 1991, Russia began the free privatization of housing. An apartment that could not be sold for forty years turned into a commodity with a single signature.
ep01.s03.fact: The Law “On the Privatization of the Housing Stock in the Russian Federation” was adopted on 4 July 1991
ep01.s03.l002: For lonely pensioners it became a lottery in which the prize and the sentence looked the same: a signature at the notary’s.
ep01.s03.l003: In the summer of 1993, owners of privatized apartments began disappearing in different districts of Moscow. Nobody connected the disappearances.
ep01.s04.l001: Zoya Pavlovna, I explained it to you: the state won’t process anything on its own. You need a person. I am that person.
ep01.s04.l002: And if I sign, the apartment stays mine?
ep01.s04.l003: It stays yours. A power of attorney is just a piece of paper so I can walk the offices instead of you.
ep01.s04.l004: The power of attorney was signed that same day. A week later Zoya Pavlovna was seen in the courtyard for the last time, with a bag and in her Sunday coat.
ep01.s05.l001: A report from a neighbor. A pensioner is missing, new owners with papers are living in her apartment. I have four reports like this in one month.
ep01.s05.l002: Four apartments, four missing people, four legal deals. Either a coincidence, or someone very careful.
ep01.s05.l003: Gromov. Prosecutor’s investigator. Two years on the job and not one case that started with an empty apartment.
ep01.s06.l001: The new tenants let us in without a word. The old owner’s things were put out on the balcony. Look for what a person does not leave behind when leaving of their own free will.
ep01.s06.l002: The papers can wait. The apartment can’t: tomorrow they start renovating, and there will be nothing left to examine.
ep01.mg_scene.intro: Examine the apartment. Mark the items a pensioner would not leave behind when going away for a long time.
ep01.s07.l001: Glasses, pills laid out by the hour, and a photo of her grandson behind the glass of the sideboard. People do not go south without their glasses.
ep01.s07.l002: The examination produced nothing that could not be explained. Gromov wrote: “no signs of a struggle found”.
ep01.s07.l003: The power of attorney was certified by notary Kovrigin on Presnya. The sale contract came two weeks later, at the same office.
ep01.doc.power_of_attorney: POWER OF ATTORNEY. I, Zoya Pavlovna S., authorize Sergei Viktorovich Murashov to represent my interests in matters of privatization and disposal of the apartment… Certified by notary A. N. Kovrigin, 14 June 1993.
ep01.mg_docs.intro: Compare the power of attorney and the contract. Find two discrepancies.
ep01.s08.l001: The date on the power of attorney has been altered. The notary certified the document retroactively.
ep01.s08.l002: The papers are clean. Too clean for a woman who never left the house without her neighbor.
ep01.s08.l003: There’s a buyer, a certain Lapin, moved in with his family. There’s the notary. Who do we lean on first?
ep01.s09.l001: I bought it through a newspaper ad! I gave the money to the middleman, the notary handled the papers. What did I do wrong?
ep01.s09.l002: You’re living in the apartment of a woman nobody has seen for two months.
ep01.s09.c_buyer.prompt: Lapin is scared and, it seems, not lying.
ep01.s09.c_buyer.detain: Hold him for three days until he remembers the middleman
ep01.s09.c_buyer.release: Release him and get a description of the middleman
ep01.s10.l001: Three days produced nothing. Lapin came out with his health broken and a firm resolve never to talk to the police again.
ep01.s10.l002: Lapin described the middleman: tall, well-spoken, “a former journalist”. Called himself Sergei.
ep01.s10.l003: We lost two weeks. Now six people are missing.
ep01.s11.l001: Record cards for every apartment that changed hands over the summer. Look for repeats: notary, attorney-in-fact, buyer.
ep01.mg_db.intro: Find every deal in the card index where the same names repeat.
ep01.s12.l001: Six deals. One notary. The same attorney-in-fact every time: “S. V. Murashov”. That’s not a coincidence. That’s a conveyor belt.
ep01.s12.l002: There are repeats, but the archive is incomplete. We’ll have to go to Kovrigin with what we have.
ep01.s12.l003: Murashov. Former journalist. Rented a room on Presnya, then suddenly: three apartments and a Volga.
ep01.doc.bti_card: BTI. Record card. Molodogvardeyskaya St. Owner: Zoya Pavlovna S. Basis of transfer: sale contract dated 28.06.1993, notary A. N. Kovrigin. Seller’s representative by power of attorney: S. V. Murashov.
ep01.s13.l001: Back then we didn’t understand that an apartment was no longer a home. It was money sitting in an old man’s pocket without him knowing. But someone knew.
ep01.s13.l002: The most frightening thing in that case wasn’t him. The most frightening thing was that the paperwork was in order.
ep01.s14.l001: By October, six folders lay on Gromov’s desk, and they had to be turned into a single case.
ep01.mg_board.intro: Connect the deals, the people and the property on the board so that the chain leads to one person.
ep01.s15.l001: He’s in the office. The second one is with him, the one who went to the showings with him. Do we take both now, or wait until they split up?
ep01.s16a.l001: Murashov’s accomplice fired once. The bullet grazed Saiko’s shoulder. Murashov was taken on the stairs; he did not say a word.
ep01.s16b.l001: The accomplice was taken by the metro an hour later. He started talking before they reached the station. Murashov was taken at his doorway, in silence.
ep01.s17.l001: You’re the investigator? Good. I like it when people work by the book. All my papers are in order.
ep01.s17.l002: He spoke like a man who had already won.
ep01.mg_interrogation.intro: Present evidence against his statements. Three mistakes and he stops talking.
ep01.s18.l001: They would have died anyway. I just made sure the apartments didn’t go to waste. I just clean up.
ep01.s18.l002: Prove it. The powers of attorney are genuine, the deals are registered. The old people left. Where to is not my concern.
ep01.s18.l003: The deals, yes. The dates, Kovrigin and your accomplice, not anymore.
ep01.s19.l001: The court found Murashov guilty of murders committed for gain and sentenced him to the exceptional measure of punishment.
ep01.s19.fact: A moratorium on the death penalty has been in force in Russia since 1996
ep01.s19.l002: Notary Kovrigin received six years. The accomplice, twelve. Returning the apartments to the heirs took another three years.
ep01.s20.l001: The apartment on Molodogvardeyskaya was returned to Zoya Pavlovna’s heirs. The Lapins moved out on their own, without waiting for the trial.
ep01.s20.l002: Viktor Saiko returned to duty four months later. He could no longer raise his right arm above the shoulder.
ep01.s20.l003: Viktor Saiko received a commendation and a new unit: “apartment” cases were now coming in a steady stream.
ep01.s20.l004: Lapin never testified in court. The count concerning his apartment was dropped from the indictment.
ep01.s20.l005: Lapin’s testimony became the basis of the fourth count. His family was given a room in a workers’ hostel.
ep01.s21.l001: Case closed. Six apartments, six names, six folders, and not a single unaccounted signature.
ep01.doc.newspaper: Vechernyaya Moskva, 1994. “The Apartment Conveyor Belt Has Been Stopped.” The investigation into the case of former journalist M. is complete: six counts have been proven…
ep01.s22.l001: Case closed. But every closed case has a price, and it is not paid by the one sitting in the cage.
ep01.s23.l001: The case was withdrawn and handed over to the city prosecutor’s office. Gromov was transferred to economic crimes.
ep01.s23.fact: The case was brought to trial in 1994 by a different investigative team. The epilogue is unavailable.

ep01.mg_interrogation.title: Interrogation
ep01.mg_interrogation.brief: Choose the evidence that refutes the statement. Evidence you did not find is unavailable.
ep01.mg_interrogation.st.dates: The power of attorney was executed on June fourteenth, in the owner’s presence, as required.
ep01.mg_interrogation.st.alone: I worked alone. I never had any helpers.
ep01.mg_interrogation.st.once: That was the only deal where I acted as attorney-in-fact.
ep01.mg_interrogation.st.south: She went south to her relatives. She said so herself.
ep01.arc.privatization.title: Housing Privatization
ep01.arc.privatization.text: The Russian law “On the Privatization of the Housing Stock” of 4 July 1991 allowed apartments to be transferred free of charge into citizens’ ownership. By the mid-90s the apartment had become the main asset of most families, and the main motive for “apartment” murders.

ep01.arc.photo.text: A snapshot behind the sideboard glass. The only thing left of the former owner in the apartment on Molodogvardeyskaya.
